name: Texas Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: BBQ, Tex-Mex & Taquerías
description:
Texas restaurants, from brisket on butcher paper to a breakfast taco on a flour tortilla.

Texas Eats is a free guide to eating in Texas: 74 barbecue joints, 55 taquerías, 30 Tex-Mex kitchens, 22 kolache bakeries and 19 chicken-fried steak plates we checked by hand, plus 78,609 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 1,233 towns, from Houston, Dallas and San Antonio to El Paso and Beaumont. No account, no ads.

TEXAS GUIDES
• Barbecue Joints: brisket, ribs and sausage.
• Taquerías: trompo to breakfast tacos.
• Tex-Mex: enchiladas, fajitas and combination plates.
• Kolaches: kolache bakeries and Czech-Texan stops on I-35 and beyond.
• Chicken-Fried Steak: with cream gravy.
• MICHELIN & James Beard: the MICHELIN Guide Texas selection and James Beard honorees (166 places).
• Oldest Places: 9 restaurants open at the same address since 1960 or earlier.
• Brewpubs and Bar Sales: places with a TABC brewpub license, and the alcohol sales the Texas Comptroller publishes.
• Inspection Scores: the latest score Austin, El Paso and Arlington publish, with each city's own band and date.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "brisket lockhart", "kolache west", "trompo".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source: the place's own site or menu, dated local news or an official tourism listing. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by a reliability rule tested against Austin's, El Paso's and Arlington's inspection lists, plus restaurants and bars from TABC's license list. Texas has no statewide grade; where those three cities publish a score, the app shows it with the city's own band and date. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Texas Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of Texas, TABC, the Texas Comptroller, or the cities of Austin, El Paso and Arlington), or with the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation. MICHELIN and the MICHELIN Guide are trademarks of Michelin. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Texas Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Texas (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: 74 barbecue joints, 55 taquerías, 30 Tex-Mex kitchens, 22 kolache bakeries and 19 chicken-fried steak plates, each checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus 166 MICHELIN Guide and James Beard honorees. It also lists 78,609 restaurants, cafés and bars statewide from open map data, checked against city inspection lists and the state's alcohol licenses. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Barbecue Joints (or Tex-Mex, Taquerías, Kolaches, Chicken-Fried Steak, MICHELIN & James Beard, Oldest Places, Brewpubs, Bar Sales, Inspection Scores, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down are the place's TABC license and, in Austin, El Paso and Arlington, the city's latest inspection score with its date.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("brisket lockhart", "kolache west", "trompo").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Texas (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Texas, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "TX Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Texas Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Texas Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); TABC's license list and the Texas Comptroller's mixed beverage sales; Austin's, El Paso's and Arlington's published inspection scores (public records); MICHELIN Guide and James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites and local news.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://texas.eatsranked.com/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Texas; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. Inspection scores appear only where Austin, El Paso or Arlington publish them, with the city's own band and date; the app computes no grades and ranks nothing by inspections. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the MICHELIN Guide or the James Beard Foundation.
